comment:
Written against commit d288900, the last commit whose plugin.json carries 2.13.0; the next commit, 03acb46, bumps the version to 2.14.0. Several dozen commits carry 2.13.0, all of them adding effects rather than changing the Rack module, so the installed build was used to settle which one shipped: PointyDeluxe, PunchyDeluxe and kBeyond are all added in d288900 and all three names are present in it.

Every parameter knob, scale knob and CV jack is described by one line because the module reuses the same ten rows for whatever effect is chosen. What a given row means is set by the effect, not by the panel, which is why no range is quoted for the parameter knobs: the knob is 0 to 1 internally (src-rack/Module.cpp:153) and each effect converts that to its own units and its own printed name (src-rack/Module.cpp:218-228 via getParameterName at :221). The census names the knobs Replace, Brightness, Detune, Bigness and Dry/Wet because those are Galactic's parameter names and a fresh module comes up on Galactic (src-rack/Module.cpp:162).

Parameters 10 and 21 are declared, named Unused, and given no widget (src-rack/Module.cpp:83-89 and :142-143), so neither can be clicked and neither gets a line. They are placeholders kept so that older patches still load.

CV inputs 10 and 11 exist as jacks but no effect has more than ten parameters, and the CV loop is bounded by that count, so the last two jacks are never read. The maker names them Unused CV.

The manual says the module holds 300 or more effects; the shipped build registers 456 of them (src/ModuleAdd.h at d288900). The manual also says the ordering setting applies to the menus, which is right for the Rack module: the arrow buttons always walk the alphabetical-within-category order (src-rack/Module.cpp:1058 calling AirwinRegistry::neighborIndexFor), and only the JUCE build's jog buttons follow the Chris order.

The effect selector, the arrow buttons and the question mark are plain widgets rather than parameters, so none of them can be clicked for help; they are covered by Note lines instead. The Light Mode and Dark Mode menu items are left out as cosmetic.
